sam-cs: FYI customer tenant 'acme-inc' is seeing short bursts of 502s on the hosted generate streaming endpoint since ~09:05 UTC. Mostly during big batch uploads. They gave trace id abc123def45. Repro with 10 parallel streaming connections reproduces a 30s window of 502s. Any quick ideas? :eyes:

anna-support: thanks — can you paste the trace and a small log snippet? also which region/model are they hitting?

sam-cs: region us-east-1, model redwood-4x, trace=abc123def45

sam-cs: ```
edge-req-id=abc123def45 level=warn msg=upstream response failed status=502 upstream_addr=10.0.4.22:443 error="upstream connect error or disconnect"
edge-req-id=abc123def46 level=error msg=rate-limiter call failed err="connection refused"
```

anna-support: ok that rate-limiter error looks interesting. tagging SRE. @mike-sre can you see any backend errors around 09:04-09:06?

mike-sre: seeing a small window of Redis master failover events in us-east-1 starting 09:04:58 UTC with increased p99 latency for ~15s. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/redirect/redis-us-east1 (snapshot). Also saw our rate-limiter client throw timeouts and the client circuit-breaker opened briefly. Likely correlation.

rediswatch-bot: Redis cluster 'rl-cluster-us-east-1' triggered failover at 2026-03-17T09:04:58Z, election duration 12s, clients saw MOVED/ASK and connection resets.

jeni-runtime: this pattern rings a bell — our RL (tenant rate-limit) client is configured with a tight RPC timeout (50ms) and we treat any error as definitive deny. When the RL errors while Redis is failing over, the auth/edge path returns 502 instead of letting requests through or queueing. Two quick mitigations:
- set RL client to fail-open for hosted API (allow request when RL unavailable)
- bump client timeout to 200ms and add short local cache for tenant token keys

I can push a short-lived config override to fail-open for the hosted tier.

ops-bot: deploy: config-change/rl-fail-open pushed to staging at 2026-03-17T09:08:12Z by jeni-runtime

mike-sre: after fail-open flip, 502s dropped by ~85% in the next 60s. Still seeing a handful of 502s tied to remaining in-flight connections that had upstream errors. Full root cause: Redis failover + aggressive RL timeouts + treating RL errs as hard denies at the edge.

sam-cs: customer reports errors mostly stopped after your change, still saw a tiny blip at 09:06:10. They're asking for a postmortem and what we'll do to prevent recurrence.

jeni-runtime: follow-ups:
- create ticket INF-12345 to add short TTL client-side cache for RL keys and increase timeout defaults
- change RL client behaviour to fail-open for hosted tier, with telemetry to count how often it happens
- add a small retry on RL reads (2 quick attempts)

mike-sre: agree. also plan to harden Redis observability and alert on failover frequency. i'll attach traces and p95/p99 numbers to INF-12345.

anna-support: I'll update the customer with the temporary mitigation and the follow-up plan.

sam-cs: thanks all. marking as monitored — will re-open if customer sees more 502s. :thumbsup:

mike-sre: short summary for postmortem: 1) Redis failover caused transient errors on RL RPCs. 2) RL client timeout + fail-closed semantics caused edge to surface 502s. 3) Mitigation: flip to fail-open, increase timeouts, add caching & retries.

rediswatch-bot: note logged: failover event correlated with request spike, id=ev-20260317-090458

ops-bot: action items created: INF-12345 (RL client changes), OBS-6789 (Redis alert tuning)

jeni-runtime: will schedule a config roll with safer defaults next week and add an integration test for RL failover.

anna-support: customer update drafted, sending now. :email:

sam-cs: closing thread for now — keep me posted on INF-12345.
